_meta.description: DISPOSABLE proof-of-concept flow. Confirms two things before the production Appraisal Review Extractor flow/topic are rebuilt around Execute Agent: (1) whether a file attached via Execute Agent's advanced 'attachments' parameter can actually be read inside a Copilot Studio topic, and (2) the real shape of Execute Agent and wait's response — is there really a 'lastResponse' field, does it need json() to parse, what else is on the response body. This flow deliberately surfaces the RAW response alongside the assumed parse, so a single test run answers the question even if the 'lastResponse' assumption turns out wrong. Delete this flow, agent/poc-attachment-echo-topic.yaml, and the throwaway PoC agent once both questions are answered.
connectors: Microsoft Copilot Studio (shared_CopilotStudio or your tenant's equivalent connector id) — Execute Agent and wait, against a THROWAWAY PoC agent, not the production one
Microsoft Teams (shared_teams) — Post message in a channel, purely so the result is easy to eyeball without opening run history
_meta.buildNote: Build the 'Execute Agent and wait' action from the live connector picker in Power Automate, not by pasting this file's 'actions.Execute_Agent_And_Wait' block — the exact operation path/schema for this action is not something this repo has verified against a real tenant yet; that is the entire point of this PoC. See POC.md for the build steps and what each possible outcome means.

trigger.description: 'Manually trigger a flow' with a File-type input, same mechanism the production design uses — reusing it here also incidentally re-confirms the Teams file-upload-to-flow path still works.

Build_Data_Uri.description: Bot Framework Attachment objects commonly reference inline content via a contentUrl data URI — this is a best guess at the format Execute Agent's attachments parameter expects, based on secondhand blog descriptions, not verified first-party docs. If the live designer's 'attachments' field wants something else (e.g. raw contentBytes instead of a data URI), build it that way instead and treat this Compose as wrong.

Execute_Agent_And_Wait.description: PLACEHOLDER — build this action from the connector picker: search 'Copilot Studio' > 'Execute Agent and wait'. Point it at the throwaway PoC agent (not production). Message/body: the literal text 'poc echo attachment' (must match the PoC topic's trigger phrase exactly). Under Advanced parameters, find the attachments field and supply one attachment: name = testFileFileName, contentType = application/pdf, contentUrl/content = the output of Build_Data_Uri. The 'path' below is not a real, verified operation id — do not paste this action, build it live.

Compose_Raw_Response.description: The whole, unmodified response body from Execute Agent and wait — inspect this first. It tells you the real field names regardless of whether the 'lastResponse' assumption below is right.

Attempt_Parse_LastResponse.description: Best-effort attempt at the pattern found in secondhand research: json(body(...)?['lastResponse']). If this action fails in run history, that itself is informative — it means either the field isn't called lastResponse, or its content wasn't valid JSON text. Check Compose_Raw_Response's output in that case rather than trying to fix this expression blindly.

Post_Raw_Result_To_Teams.description: Always posts the raw response — this alone is enough to answer question 2 (the real field names/shape), regardless of whether the lastResponse parse attempt below succeeds.

Post_Parsed_Result_To_Teams.description: Separate, independent post — only fires if Attempt_Parse_LastResponse actually succeeded. If this message never arrives but Post_Raw_Result_To_Teams's does, that itself is the finding: 'lastResponse' isn't the real field, or its content isn't valid JSON text. Check the raw response message for the actual field name to use instead.

notificationChannelId.description: Any channel you can post test results to — does not need to be the real credit risk channel.
